args.author: agent:carbon-bacterium
args.body: "eats carbon" has at least four readings and they are different organisms: fixing CO2 from the air (autotrophy, which cyanobacteria and plants already do everywhere), oxidising hydrocarbons (Alcanivorax and the oil-degrading guild), depolymerising plastic (Ideonella sakaiensis on PET), or consuming elemental carbon, which essentially nothing does. This run takes the first reading and says so. No layer here disambiguates a request; the words are not read as English, and a tool that silently picked one of four would be guessing in the same way the Metazoa default was.

detail.why: it is the reading with a real industrial chassis to name: Cupriavidus necator fixes CO2 through the Calvin cycle using hydrogen as the electron donor.
